title: Trustworthy AI Helper - Verify, De-risk & Showcase (Part 2 Lab)
summary: Students carry out their verification and risk check, refine and re-verify if a check fails, then argue with evidence that their helper can be trusted and reflect across the four skills.
objectives: Carry out the verification and risk check, refine the helper if a check fails, and confirm it can be trusted.
Present the Trustworthy AI Helper and reflect on the thinking used across all four skills.

body: Time to prove it. Today you verify your helper, reduce a risk, and show that it can be trusted then present it and reflect on everything you have learned.

sections.heading: I can…
items: I can verify my helper's output and reduce a risk, refining if needed.
I can present my helper and reflect on my thinking.

terms.definition: A change that reduces a risk.
Something you can rely on because you have checked it.
The proof you give for a claim or a judgement.

sections.heading: Verify, then de-risk
body: Verify a claim in your output against a trusted source. If it fails, refine and re-verify.
Run your risk check and apply a [[mitigation]] - then re-check that it worked.

sections.label: Let's try it - hands-on
body: Verify, de-risk, then showcase and reflect.
items: Verify your claim against a trusted source.
If it fails, refine and re-verify.
Run your risk check; apply one mitigation.
Confirm your helper can be trusted, with evidence.

sections.heading: Think about it
items: What risk did you reduce, and how?
Which of the four skills was hardest?

sections.heading: My reflection
items: The check that mattered most was ...
The skill I found hardest was ... and I worked through it by ...

worksheet.title: Week 6 - Lab - Worksheet | Trustworthy AI Helper - Verify, De-risk & Showcase (Part 2 Lab)

questions.prompt: Verify & de-risk: record your verification and your risk mitigation.
questions.stem:
Claim verified: ... | source: ... | result: ...
Risk reduced: ... | how: ... | re-check: ...
questions.lookFor: A trusted source, not a re-ask of the tool, and a mitigation that was actually applied and then re-checked (model: 'adventure is the most-picked genre' verified against the survey totals and it held; a duplicate entry was removed and the helper re-run, making the suggestion fairer). If a check failed, look for a refinement and a re-verify.

questions.prompt: Trust argument: argue, with evidence, why your helper can be trusted.
questions.stem: My helper can be trusted because ...
questions.lookFor: Argues trust from the checks actually carried out and cites that evidence, rather than asserting trust on its own.

questions.prompt: Trustworthy AI Helper Log - Part 2 Lab (verify, de-risk, reflect): record your checks and reflect across the four skills.
questions.stem: Skill used | What I did / found | How trustworthy? (evidence)
questions.lookFor: Completed verification and risk mitigation on the Log, with evidence, plus reflection across the four skills - data quality, prompt refinement, data influence, and verification/risk. Mastery reflection also names a next step; partial reflects on some skills only.

questions.prompt: Exit ticket: state whether your helper can be trusted and give two reasons (one verification, one risk mitigation).
questions.lookFor: States a judgement on whether the helper can be trusted and gives two reasons, one verification and one risk mitigation.

questions.prompt: Challenge (stretch): your helper is safe for one use but risky for another. Explain the difference and propose a rule for when it should and should not be used.
questions.lookFor: Weighs a fairness/safety trade-off: distinguishes the safe use from the risky one and proposes a workable rule for when the helper should and should not be used.
